title: Design Your Dungeon Room
pageTitle: Represent Polygons on the Coordinate Plane
covers: how to draw a polygon from its vertex coordinates, find side lengths from coordinates, and tell perimeter (the distance around) from area (the space inside)
cert: drawing polygons from vertices and using coordinates to find side lengths, perimeter and area

intro.caption: Lesson 7-7 — polygons on the coordinate plane. Grimble is running a contest: design the best new room for Floor −7. The prize is a golden cup. The party has one map and four corners to place.

balloons.t: A room is a polygon. We plot each corner, each vertex, and connect them in order.
Ooh, a camp room! With walls! And a rug! Do not let Kwame order the rug.
Best room wins my golden cup! Only slightly fake gold.
Our corners: (−4, 3), (2, 3), (2, −1) and (−4, −1). Connect them in order and we get a rectangle.

pages.caption: Every vertex is an ordered pair: x first, across; y second, up or down. Then connect the vertices in order to close the shape.

balloons.t: Four pins, four corners. x across first, then y!
The top wall goes from (−4, 3) to (2, 3). Same y, so it's flat. How long is it?
−4 and 2 are on opposite sides of zero. I think we add.
The walls add up to 20, so I bought 20 rug squares! Why is the floor... OPENING?
20 is the way AROUND. A rug covers the INSIDE. Those are different numbers.

pages.caption: Perimeter is the distance around a polygon, the sum of its side lengths. Area is the number of unit squares inside it.

balloons.t: Last room: a treasure vault. Fence it, and tell me the fence in METERS. Each grid unit is 2 meters.
A scale! Count units first, then change to meters.
I am never buying a rug by the perimeter again.
20 units of crystal fence, 24 rug squares, zero trapdoors. Best room on the floor!

win.caption: Plot the vertices, connect them in order, and use coordinates to find each side. Add the sides for the perimeter. Multiply length × width for a rectangle's area.

gates.title: Gate 1 · Plot the Vertices
gates.prompt: Pin the four corners of the camp room: (−4, 3), (2, 3), (2, −1) and (−4, −1).
hints: Conceptual: each vertex is an ordered pair. The first number moves you across, the second moves you up or down.
Procedural: start at (0, 0) for each point. Move left or right by x, then up or down by y. Negative means left or down.

steps: (5, 1): go right 5, up 1. (5, 4): right 5, up 4. (1, 4): right 1, up 4.
Connect them in order and the last side goes back to (1, 1). The shape is a rectangle.
worked.q: A rectangle has vertices (−3, 2), (1, 2) and (1, −2). What is the fourth vertex?

items.q: Tap all four corners of the camp room.

fb.msg: That's (3, −4): x and y are swapped. For (−4, 3), go left 4 first, then up 3.
That's (3, 2): x and y are swapped. For (2, 3), go right 2 first, then up 3.
That's (−1, 2): x and y are swapped. For (2, −1), go right 2 first, then down 1.
That's (−1, −4): x and y are swapped. For (−4, −1), go left 4 first, then down 1.
That's (4, 3). The x is −4, so go LEFT 4, not right.

items.fbDefault: Check each corner: x across first, then y up or down. You need exactly four points.

items.q: Which vertex is joined to (2, 3) by a vertical wall?

options.fb: (−4, 3) shares the y-coordinate 3, so that wall is horizontal, not vertical.
(−4, −1) shares no coordinate with (2, 3). It is the opposite corner.
(3, 2) is not a vertex of this room. It is (2, 3) with x and y swapped.

gates.pass: Four glowing pins, four straight walls. The room is a rectangle, and Grimble squints at it suspiciously.

gates.title: Gate 2 · Side Lengths
gates.prompt: Use the coordinates to find how long each wall is. No measuring rope needed.
hints: Conceptual: two vertices on the same wall share one coordinate. The OTHER coordinate tells you how long the wall is.
Procedural: take the absolute values of the coordinates that change. Opposite signs: add them. Same sign: subtract.

steps: Practice wall: (−5, 1) to (−1, 1). The y's match, so the wall is horizontal.
−5 and −1 are both negative, on the same side of zero.
worked.q: How long is the wall from (3, −5) to (3, 2)?

items.label: Top wall · (−4, 3) to (2, 3):
items.aria: length of the top wall in units

fb.msg: That's 4 − 2. The x's −4 and 2 are on opposite sides of zero, so add: 4 + 2.
A side length is never negative. It is 6 units.
The y's are both 3, so the wall is flat. Look at the x's, −4 and 2.

items.fbDefault: The y's match. Find the distance from x = −4 to x = 2.

items.label: Right wall · (2, 3) to (2, −1):
items.aria: length of the right wall in units

fb.msg: That's 3 − 1. The y's 3 and −1 are on opposite sides of the x-axis, so add: 3 + 1.
A side length is never negative. It is 4 units.
The x's are both 2, so the wall is vertical. Look at the y's, 3 and −1.

items.fbDefault: The x's match. Find the distance from y = 3 to y = −1.

gates.pass: The room is 6 units wide and 4 units tall. Anya coils up the measuring rope: they never needed it.

gates.title: Gate 3 · Perimeter or Area?
gates.prompt: The room is 6 units by 4 units. The crystal fence goes AROUND the walls. The rug covers the whole FLOOR.
hints: Conceptual: perimeter measures the edge (a length). Area counts the unit squares inside (a space). Ask: around, or inside?
Procedural: perimeter = add all four sides. Area of a rectangle = length × width.

steps: Perimeter: 5 + 3 + 5 + 3 = 16 units of fence around it.
Area: 5 × 3 = 15 unit squares of rug inside it.
worked.q: A room is 7 units by 2 units. What is its perimeter?

items.q: Sol puts a crystal fence along every wall. Which measurement tells how much fence she needs?

options.fb: Area counts the squares inside the room. A fence runs along the edge, so you need the distance around.
The fence goes along every wall, not just one. Add all four sides.
The room has 4 vertices, but a fence is a length. Add the side lengths.

items.label: Crystal fence (perimeter), units:
items.aria: perimeter of the room in units

fb.msg: 24 is 6 × 4, the AREA: squares inside. The fence goes around, so add the four sides.
10 is only two sides, 6 + 4. A rectangle has four sides: add the other two.

items.label: Rug squares (area):
items.aria: area of the room in square units

fb.msg: 20 is the perimeter, the distance around. That's Kwame's rug, and it left a hole. Count the squares inside.
10 is 6 + 4. Area does not add the sides. Count the squares: 4 rows of 6.

items.fbDefault: The floor has 4 rows of 6 squares. Multiply 6 × 4.

gates.pass: 20 units of crystal fence and a 24-square rug. Kwame rolls out the new rug and the trapdoor stays shut.

gates.title: Boss Gate · Grimble's Judging Desk
gates.prompt: The treasure vault has three corners: (1, −2), (5, −2) and (5, −5). It is a rectangle. Each grid unit is 2 meters.
hints: Conceptual: a rectangle's opposite sides match, so the missing corner shares an x with one vertex and a y with another.
Procedural: find the side lengths in units first. Add them for the perimeter. Then multiply the units by the scale to get meters.

steps: Practice: a rectangle is 2 units by 6 units, and each unit is 5 meters.
worked.q: Each unit is 10 meters. A side is 3 units long. How long is it in meters?

items.q: Tap the fourth corner of the vault.

fb.msg: That's (−5, 1): x and y are swapped. The corner sits below (1, −2), so x = 1 and y = −5.
Right x, wrong sign on y. The vault is below the x-axis, so y = −5.
Right y, wrong sign on x. The corner sits straight below (1, −2), so x = 1.

items.fbDefault: The missing corner shares x with (1, −2) and y with (5, −5).

items.label: Vault perimeter, in units:
items.aria: perimeter of the vault in grid units

fb.msg: 12 is 4 × 3, the AREA. The fence goes around: add the four sides.
7 is only two sides, 4 + 3. Add all four sides.
Check the width: x goes from 1 to 5, both positive, so it's 5 − 1 = 4, not 6.

items.fbDefault: Width: 5 − 1 = 4 units. Height: 5 − 2 = 3 units. Add all four sides.

items.label: Vault fence, in meters:
items.aria: perimeter of the vault in meters

fb.msg: 14 is the perimeter in grid units. Each unit is 2 meters, so multiply by 2.
24 is the area, 12, times 2. The fence is the perimeter: 14 units × 2 meters.
48 is the floor space in square meters, 8 × 6. The fence is a length around the edge.

items.fbDefault: Find the perimeter in units, then multiply by 2 meters per unit.

gates.pass: Vault corner (1, −5), 14 units around, 28 meters of fence. Grimble drops his monocle and hands over the golden cup.

journal.heading: Lesson 7-7 — what the dungeon room taught us
rows: Each corner is an ordered pair. Plot (−4, 3), (2, 3), (2, −1), (−4, −1) and connect them in order to close the polygon.
Two vertices on one side share a coordinate. (−4, 3) to (2, 3): opposite signs, so 4 + 2 = 6 units.
Perimeter goes AROUND: 6 + 4 + 6 + 4 = 20 units. Area fills the INSIDE: 6 × 4 = 24 square units.
If one grid unit is 2 meters, a 14-unit fence is 14 × 2 = 28 meters.
He bought 20 rug squares because the walls added to 20. A rug needs the area, 24, so 4 squares were missing.
journal.quote: "Around is a fence. Inside is a rug. Kwame, write that down." — Pip

teacher.suggested: Use during or after lesson 7-7 (Represent Polygons on the Coordinate Plane) as one focused read. Whole-class on a projector, pairs on devices, or independent practice. It covers only this lesson: plotting polygon vertices, finding side lengths from coordinates that share an x or a y, perimeter and area of rectangles on the plane, and using a scale.
standards: Draw polygons in the coordinate plane from vertex coordinates; use coordinates to find side lengths and solve problems
